linkedin.title: Most people feel overwhelmed by the news, not informed.
linkedin.body:
We live in an era of infinite content, yet finding what actually matters to your specific life feels harder than ever. The current model relies on engagement metrics that prioritize outrage and broad appeal. This approach treats every reader the same, which is a mistake.

True personalization is not about creating a filter bubble that hides the world. It is about respecting your time and your intelligence. It means delivering the stories that connect to your professional interests, your curiosity, and your goals, without the noise of irrelevant updates.

When we use AI to curate news, we are not trying to replace human judgment. We are trying to augment it. A system that learns what you value allows you to stay informed on the topics that shape your industry and your world, rather than just reacting to the loudest headlines of the day.

We believe the future of news is quiet, relevant, and centered on the individual reader. It is time to stop scrolling through endless feeds and start reading what actually moves the needle for you.

story_card.headline: Cyberattack hits French supermarket fridges
story_card.standfirst: Hundreds of stores are dealing with spoiled inventory after an overnight digital hack.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: A cyberattack targeted supermarket refrigeration systems across France overnight.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Hackers breached the store networks. This caused the cooling systems to fail entirely.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The failure ruined massive amounts of fresh and frozen food worth millions of euros.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Authorities are investigating the scope of the damage and who is responsible.

story_card.caption:
A major cyberattack on French supermarket cooling systems has caused millions of euros in food waste.

Hundreds of locations were hit by the hack, which knocked out refrigeration overnight. This serves as a stark reminder of how vulnerable modern supply chains are to digital interference.
